question.problem:
A certain store sells three types of instant soups: chicken, meat, and vegetable. The following table describes how the number of customers changes between the three types of instant soups each month:
From:
Chicken Meat Vegetable
To: Chicken $0.4$ $0.2$ $0.3$
Meat $0.3$ $0.4$ $0.2$
Vegetable $0.3$ $0.4$ $0.5$
For example, $30%$ of chicken soup customers switch to vegetable each month, and $20%$ of vegetable customers switch to meat. Currently, $400$ customers buy chicken soup, $400$ customers buy meat soup, and $200$ customers buy vegetable soup. How many customers will purchase vegetable instant soup in one month? You may assume that the total number of customers doesn't change.
question.worked_solution:
From the table, we can build the corresponding stochastic matrix: 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}0.4 & 0.2 & 0.3 \\ 0.3 & 0.4 & 0.2 \\ 0.3 & 0.4 & 0.5\end{aligned}]
$$

The vector describing the number of customers for each type of instant soup is

$$
[\begin{aligned}400 \\ 400 \\ 200\end{aligned}].
$$

Dividing the vector above by the total number of customers $(1\,000),$ we get the stochastic vector of the initial state:

$$
{x}_{0}=\frac{1}{1\,000}[\begin{aligned}400 \\ 400 \\ 200\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0.4 \\ 0.4 \\ 0.2\end{aligned}]
$$

To find the state vector ${x}_{1}$ after one month, we apply one step of the Markov chain:

$$
{x}_{1}=P{x}_{0}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =P{x}_{0} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0.4 & 0.2 & 0.3 \\ 0.3 & 0.4 & 0.2 \\ 0.3 & 0.4 & 0.5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0.4 \\ 0.4 \\ 0.2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0.3 \\ 0.32 \\ 0.38\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, after one month, $38%$ of customers will buy vegetable soup. Computing $38%$ of $1\,000,$ we obtain

$$
1\,000\cdot 0.38=380.
$$

Therefore, $380$ customers will buy vegetable instant soup in one month.
